For local unsynced checkpoints: upload scoped transcript material to the entire.io API for on-demand analysis (see [RFD-014 CLI Flow for Local Unsynced Checkpoints](https://github.com/entirehq/company-knowledge/pull/76)). The uploaded payload is minimal: checkpoint-scoped transcript, prompt, files touched, checkpoint ID, repo identity, and agent metadata.

   446	7. Ask the LLM for structured memories using the production schema.
   447	8. Apply preset admission gates.

   511	**Degraded-mode behavior (API unreachable):**
   512	
   513	- Cached entries within 48 hours of `fetched_at` may still be used for memory generation. These are recent enough that the analysis is unlikely to have been corrected server-side.

   520	### API Authorization and Cache Binding
   521	
   522	**Server-side authorization:**
   523

   526	- `POST /analysis` (unsynced upload) verifies the authenticated user has write access to the repo. The API resolves repo identity from its own records or the GitHub App installation, not from the client-supplied `owner/repo` string alone.

   530

   532	- Synced checkpoint fetches use `GET /analysis?checkpoint_id=<id>&repo_id=<id>`.
   533	- Unsynced checkpoint uploads use `POST /analysis` with the scoped payload.
   534	- The API response must include `checkpoint_id`, `repo_id`, and `schema_version` fields that match the request. The CLI rejects responses where any of these do not match. Echoed IDs are a client-side safety check, not a substitute for server-side authorization.

   542	**Rejection behavior:**
   543	
   544	- If the API returns an analysis for a different `checkpoint_id` or `repo_id` than requested, the response is discarded and logged as a warning. The checkpoint is treated as having no analysis for this refresh cycle.
   545	- If the API returns `403`, the CLI logs the denied repo and continues to the next checkpoint without caching.
   546	
   547	---
   548	
   549	## 5. Beta Decisions and Open Questions
   550	
   551	### Decided Beta Behavior
   552	
   553	- Shared repo memories are in scope for beta.
   554	- Beta defaults to `mode=auto`.
   555	- Beta defaults to `policy=review`.
   556	- Under `review`, all generated memories are `candidate`, regardless of scope.
   557	- Under `auto`, all generated memories are `active`, regardless of scope.
   558	- Generated candidate review is TUI-only in beta.
   559	- Manual memories are editable and can be created in any scope.
   560	- Generated memories are uneditable in beta.

Yes, but mostly as a source of later-stage ideas, not as the design to implement.

The rollout doc already makes stronger product decisions in a few places: it fixes the beta schema and signal model, uses local SQLite plus API-backed `CheckpointAnalysis`, and keeps the injection path very tight and local-first in [2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md#L22), [2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md#L139), [2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md#L307), and [2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md#L418). The Jumperz doc is broader and more exploratory; it’s useful for pressure-testing the roadmap, but it does not line up exactly with this rollout’s chosen architecture.

Where it does help:
- It reinforces the need for explicit memory lifecycle and retrieval discipline, which this design already has via status/state, thresholds, scoring, and reconciliation in [2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md#L57) and [2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md#L455).
- It suggests good future additions around auditability, maintenance, decay/trust, and richer retrieval. Some of that is already partially present here with `memory_history`, `injection_logs`, `refresh_history`, `source_signal`, and outcome tracking in [2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md#L196), [2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md#L205), and [2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md#L486).

Where it does not help much right now:
- It is too large for the beta rollout. This doc is intentionally shipping vertical slices and deferring complexity like auto-refresh and some shared-state decisions, as shown in [2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md#L503) and [2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md#L549).
- The rollout doc is trying to reduce noise with concrete structured fields and admission gates; the main current pain is memory quality, not missing architectural layers, per [MEMORY_QUALITY_ANALYSIS.md](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/MEMORY_QUALITY_ANALYSIS.md#L1).

Short version: useful as a “phase 2/3 inspiration” document, not a replacement for the rollout plan. If you want, I can map the Jumperz components into `fits beta now`, `fits later`, and `doesn’t fit this design`.
